title: Energy
seo_title: Year 10 Science: Energy Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Energy changes in a system and the ways energy is stored before and after such changes; kinetic energy, elastic potential energy and gravitational potential energy calculations; specific heat capacity; power; conservation and dissipation of energy; efficiency; national and global energy resources.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on energy: stores, kinetic and gravitational potential energy, elastic energy, specific heat capacity, power, efficiency and energy resources. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is never created or destroyed.
key_sub: Ek = ½mv², Ep = mgh, ΔE = mcΔθ, P = E ÷ t.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is transferred between stores; the total stays the same.

  • Kinetic energy = ½mv². Gravitational potential energy = mgh. Elastic potential energy = ½ke².
  • ΔE = mcΔθ: specific heat capacity is the energy to warm 1 kg by 1 °C.
  • Power = energy ÷ time. Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input. Wasted energy is usually dissipated as heat.
Example

2 kg at 3 m/s. Kinetic energy?

½ × 2 × 3²

Answer: 9 J

Example

1 kg of water warmed by 10 °C?

1 × 4,200 × 10

Answer: 42,000 J

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square the speed in ½mv².
  • Saying energy is used up.
  • Thinking efficiency can be over 100%.

faq.q: How do you calculate kinetic energy?
faq.a: Kinetic energy (J) = ½ × mass (kg) × speed² (m/s). Square the speed first.
The energy needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C. Use ΔE = m × c × Δθ.
Efficiency = useful energy output ÷ total energy input. Multiply by 100 for a percentage.
